based_on.title: Formalizing Computability Theory via Partial Recursive Functions
based_on.venue: 10th International Conference on Interactive Theorem Proving

summary: Number programs, build a universal evaluator, and distinguish recognizing successful computations from deciding whether they ever succeed.
abstract: A program can receive the code of another program and carry out its instructions. Numerical program codes make this precise: one partial recursive evaluator performs every partial recursive computation, and fixed inputs can be inserted into program text by a primitive-recursive transformation. The same coding also permits diagonal arguments. No total recursive procedure decides whether an arbitrary program stops, and some total recursive functions lie beyond primitive recursion. Successful computations can nevertheless be recognized from finite evidence. The sets recognized this way are the computably enumerable sets; membership becomes decidable exactly when both members and nonmembers can be recognized by such procedures.
